beeper_on.description: Enable the fan's audible confirmation beeps.

cooling_set_ideal_temp.description: Set the Smart cooling target temperature (LEARN;ZEROTEMP).

temp.description: Hundredths of a degree Celsius on the wire, whatever unit the app displays: raw = round(celsius / 0.01). 10.00-31.50 C is aiosenseme's clamp. TomFaulkner clamps 50-90 F, about the same range. The legacy vendor app's own limits are not held.

cooling_set_max_speed.description: Set the highest speed Smart cooling may use.

speed.description: 7 = no maximum. Range as the Indigo plugin validates it and aiosenseme clamps it.

cooling_set_min_speed.description: Set the lowest speed Smart cooling may use.

speed.description: 0 = no minimum. Range as the Indigo plugin validates it and aiosenseme clamps it.

discover.description: Discovery probe. Broadcast to UDP 31415; every legacy device answers with a DiscoveryReply.

fan_motion_auto_off.description: Stop the occupancy sensor switching the fan on.

fan_motion_auto_on.description: Let the occupancy sensor switch the fan on.
fan_motion_auto_on.notes: Spelling shared by aiosenseme and Indigo; TomFaulkner sends FAN;AUTO;SET;ON.

fan_set_direction.description: Set the rotation direction. REV is the vendor's winter / Heat Assist direction (air pushed up to mix warm air down).

direction.description: FWD or REV, as the wire spells them.

fan_set_room_speed_limits.description: Set the room-level speed limits (FAN;BOOKENDS). The fan keeps the same number of steps but maps them inside min..max.
fan_set_room_speed_limits.notes: Single source (aiosenseme). Not bound to an entity: a two-value write has no control shape yet.

max.description: Highest speed step, at most FAN;SPD;MAX.

min.description: Lowest speed step. Must be below max; aiosenseme refuses to send otherwise.

fan_set_speed.description: Set the fan speed step. 0 stops the fan; 1-7 run it.
fan_set_speed.notes: aiosenseme observed that setting a speed also switches Whoosh off.

speed.description: Speed step, the vendor app's seven speeds plus 0 for off. Clamp to the device's own FAN;SPD;MAX, which is 7 in every dump, as aiosenseme does. The room's FAN;BOOKENDS may narrow the usable range further.

fan_turn_on.description: Switch the fan motor on at its last speed.

fan_whoosh_on.description: Turn Whoosh on (speed varies around the current setting).
fan_whoosh_on.notes: The reply and push key is FAN;WHOOSH;STATUS.

get_all.description: Dump every setting as a burst of SenseMEReply messages. Does not include the occupancy status.

target.description: The device's MAC as it reports it.

returns.description: About 40-55 replies, depending on model (see protocol_details.senseme.state_keys).
returns.name: SenseMEReply

get_device_id.description: Ask one device for its name, MAC and model on an open connection.

target.description: ALL, the MAC, or the name. On a unicast connection before the MAC is known, aiosenseme puts the device's IP address here and gets an answer.

returns.description: Same shape as the discovery reply.
returns.name: DiscoveryReply

get_occupancy.description: Read the motion sensor. GETALL leaves it out.

identify.description: Make the device signal where it is. The current vendor app's legacy-device handler sends this for its identify action.
identify.notes: 10000 is the literal the app sends. Its unit is not established (plausibly milliseconds, a 10 s signal). Whether the device beeps, flashes or both is not established either. No open-source client sends this.

light_motion_auto_off.description: Stop the occupancy sensor switching the light on.

light_motion_auto_on.description: Let the occupancy sensor switch the light on.

light_set_color_temp.description: Set the Haiku Light's white colour temperature.
light_set_color_temp.notes: Haiku Light only. Fan light kits report no colour keys.

kelvin.description: Kelvin. The bounds are the device's own LIGHT;COLOR;TEMP;MIN/MAX in the one published dump. aiosenseme clamps to those keys and rounds to the nearest 100 K.

level.description: Brightness step. The device reports LIGHT;LEVEL;MIN 1 and MAX 16. aiosenseme, Indigo and BigAssFansAPI all accept 0-16. Prefer light_turn_off to 0 for off. Current-firmware apps show a percentage; on this protocol it is sixteen steps.

light_turn_on.description: Switch the light on at its last level.

occupancy_set_timeout.description: Set how long after the last motion the fan and light switch off.

timeout.description: Milliseconds on the wire: raw = seconds / 0.001. The bounds are the device's own SNSROCC;TIMEOUT;MIN and MAX (1 min to 24 h). TomFaulkner sends whole minutes x 60000.

set_name.notes: From the vendor app's legacy handler. Other clients read NAME;VALUE but do not write it.

name.description: The new name, with < > ; ( ) + , and backslash each preceded by a backslash (protocol_details.senseme.escaping). The maximum length is not established.

temp.description: Hundredths of a degree Celsius. 10-32 C is the range the Indigo plugin validates.

sleep_set_max_speed.description: Set the highest speed sleep mode may use.

speed.description: 0-7 per haiku-senseme. The dumps show 2 and 7.

sleep_set_min_speed.description: Set the lowest speed sleep mode may use.

speed.description: 0 = no minimum. 0-7 per haiku-senseme; TomFaulkner sends the same key.

smartmode_set.description: Choose the Smart Mode (the vendor's Auto Comfort).
smartmode_set.notes: aiosenseme and Indigo write this key. SMARTMODE;ACTUAL reports what is in effect. BigAssFansAPI and TomFaulkner drive an older LEARN;STATE key instead (on = LEARN); not declared.

mode.description: One of OFF, COOLING, HEATING, FOLLOWTSTAT.

values.COOLING: speed rises with room temperature above LEARN;ZEROTEMP
values.FOLLOWTSTAT: follow a linked thermostat between cooling and heating
values.HEATING: slow mixing while occupied, faster mixing while unoccupied (aiosenseme's description)

wifi_join.advanced_reason: Moves the device off the network the client is on. A wrong SSID or passphrase leaves it unreachable until it is factory reset and set up again from its access point.
wifi_join.description: Tell the device to leave its current network (or setup access point) and join another.
wifi_join.notes: From the vendor app's legacy handler, which sends it on its TCP connection. The reply, if any, and how a failed join shows itself are not established. How an open network is joined is not established either.

passphrase.description: Network passphrase, escaped the same way. Sent in plain text.

ssid.description: Network name, escaped as in protocol_details.senseme.escaping. 32 bytes is the 802.11 limit.

wifi_scan.description: Ask the device to scan for Wi-Fi networks, as the vendor app does during setup.
wifi_scan.notes: The reply format is not established.

identity.notes: The MAC is the discovery reply's fourth field. aiosenseme sends it back as the target of every request. NW;TOKEN (in GETALL) is a per-device UUID that aiosenseme keeps as the device's uuid. The name is user-assigned and changes. Key stored state by MAC and never by IP address.

methods.notes: The reply is one ASCII datagram, (name;DEVICE;ID;mac;model). Strip the parentheses and split on ';'. field:N counts from 0 in that split. The schema's response_format enum has no value for delimited ASCII, so the shape is in payload_formats.DiscoveryReply. Send the probe from local UDP port 31415 with SO_REUSEADDR and broadcast enabled. aiosenseme, the BigAssFansAPI client and the vendor app all bind that port. The vendor app falls back to an ephemeral source port after repeated bind failures and still expects answers, which suggests the device answers to the probe's source port (reported, not verified). aiosenseme sends to 255.255.255.255 on every IPv4 interface. The vendor app sends to the subnet-directed broadcast (address OR NOT netmask). aiosenseme repeats the probe every second for 5 s and then waits minutes before the next round. The vendor app repeats every 5 s while its device list is open. aiosenseme drops replies shorter than 31 or longer than 200 characters, replies that do not have exactly five fields, and the wall control's model string. Whether replies are unicast or broadcast is not established.

mac_prefixes.notes: Carried by the fan, Haiku Light and wall-control examples in the openHAB bigassfan binding's documentation. The block is registered to Delta Electronics (registries/ieee-oui.tsv). Delta Electronics is not Big Ass Fans' parent (Delta T LLC), so this is most likely the Wi-Fi module's maker, and the OUI covers everything that maker ships. It ranks a scan result and identifies nothing.

identification.notes: The strong signal is an answer to the UDP probe on port 31415 (see discovery). Only a SenseME device replies, and its fifth field names the model family (device.variants). No mDNS or SSDP advertisement is established for legacy firmware.

device.name: Big Ass Fans Haiku with SenseME (legacy firmware)
device.notes:
WHAT THIS IS: the local protocol of Big Ass Fans' residential Haiku line (fans, the standalone Haiku Light and the Haiku Wall Control) on the SenseME firmware that predates 3.0. A device on this firmware can be fully controlled on the LAN with no account and no cloud: power, speed 0-7, direction, Whoosh, sleep mode, Smart Mode (the vendor's "Auto Comfort") and its temperature target and speed bounds, the light level, the Haiku Light's colour temperature, and the motion (occupancy) sensor. There is no authentication of any kind: anything on the LAN can read and change every setting, rename the device or move it to another Wi-Fi network.
PORT 31415, BOTH UDP AND TCP. Discovery is a UDP broadcast of the ASCII probe <ALL;DEVICE;ID;GET> to port 31415; each device answers with one datagram (name;DEVICE;ID;<mac>;<model>). Control and state normally run over a TCP connection to port 31415. aiosenseme, openHAB, TomFaulkner's client and the current vendor app's legacy-device handler all use TCP. The Indigo plugin sends set commands as single UDP datagrams to the same port and reads state over TCP, so the device accepts a request in either form. A client that wants replies and pushed state should hold one TCP connection open.
FRAMING (protocol_details.senseme has the full grammar, per-key value counts, ranges and units). Requests are ASCII, wrapped in angle brackets, with tokens separated by semicolons: <target;CATEGORY;ATTRIBUTE;...>. The target is the device's MAC (aiosenseme, openHAB), its name (Indigo, TomFaulkner) or ALL (the discovery probe). Replies and pushed state are wrapped in parentheses: (name;CATEGORY;ATTRIBUTE;...;value). The first token of a reply is the device's name. Nothing terminates a message except its closing bracket. A TCP read can carry several replies or half of one, so buffer and split on the closing parenthesis. Free text (names, SSIDs, passphrases) escapes the eight characters < > ; ( ) + , and backslash with a backslash.
STATE: <target;GETALL> returns every setting as a burst of replies. It does not include the occupancy status, which needs its own <target;SNSROCC;STATUS;GET>. After the first read, an open TCP connection receives a reply-shaped push for every change, whatever caused it (the remote, the wall control, the vendor app, the fan's own Smart Mode loop). aiosenseme re-sends GETALL every minute and treats about 90 s of silence as a dead connection.
TWO GENERATIONS, ONE PORT NUMBER. Firmware 3.x (April 2022 onwards, and all i6 and es6 fans) replaced this protocol with a protobuf one. Per the current vendor app, it also uses TCP port 31415, and the device advertises mDNS _api._tcp. An open TCP 31415 therefore does not mean "legacy". A device that answers the UDP probe with a (name;DEVICE;ID;mac;model) datagram is the legacy signal. Accepting a firmware update from the current Big Ass Fans app moves a legacy device to 3.x. The app also has a support-directed "downgrade" path that factory-resets the device back onto legacy firmware (features[0]).
ROOM TEMPERATURE: none of the published legacy clients reads a room temperature. The fan uses one internally for Smart Mode. The room temperature the current app shows belongs to 3.x firmware. Whether a legacy GET for it exists is an open question.
MANUFACTURER STATUS: Big Ass Fans is an active company and still supports these products. The legacy protocol itself is superseded. The vendor steers legacy devices either to its older "Haiku by BAF" app or to a firmware update to 3.x.

openness.notes: Big Ass Fans never published the SenseME protocol. The community worked it out from traffic between the Haiku Home app and a Haiku fan (Bruce Pennypacker's Indigo plugin, 2015 onwards). Several clients followed, and aiosenseme became the Home Assistant library. aiosenseme was archived on 2023-06-09 because firmware 3.x replaced the protocol. The Indigo plugin is GPL-2.0 and aiosenseme is GPL-3.0; this file cites them by file and restates the protocol in its own words.

exclusivity.recovery: Nothing to clear. Several clients can hold TCP connections at once. aiosenseme was designed to keep its socket open while the vendor app and the remote are in use, and it receives their changes as pushes.

pairing.notes: Nothing pairs. The LAN protocol is unauthenticated and needs no bond, key or code. The Bluetooth wall remote pairs with the fan over BLE, but that link is a 3.x-era accessory and out of scope here.

unpair.notes: There is nothing to unpair: the protocol has no client registration. To stop a client controlling the device, take the client, or the device, off the network.

credentials.notes: The passphrase goes to the device in clear ASCII inside NW;JOIN, backslash-escaped but not encrypted, on a network with no transport security. After setup nothing authenticates a client: there is no key, token or pairing, and every command in this file works for anyone on the LAN.
stored_on_device: Device name, room name and room type
Smart Mode, sleep and motion settings, and on-device schedules
NW;TOKEN, a per-device UUID associated with the vendor cloud

factory_reset.description: No legacy-specific reset procedure is held. The candidate below is the current vendor app's remote-control reset, written for fans on current firmware. Legacy Haiku fans shipped with an infrared remote, and the sequence may differ on them. The Haiku L installation guide's remote REBOOT is a different thing and does not clear settings: hold fan On/Off until the LEDs blink, then press it again within 30 s. No protocol message that resets the device is known.
factory_reset.effect: Per the current vendor app, a factory-reset device loses its network connection and must be added again. Per the i6 manual, for the i6, a reset erases fan names and Wi-Fi settings. Whether a legacy reset also clears room membership, schedules and Smart Mode settings is not established.

procedures.basis: The reset instructions in the current Big Ass Fans app (3.3.4 and 3.4.0). Hold Fan Power about 5 s until the LEDs blink and the fan beeps, then tap Speed Minus or Speed Plus (the app shows one or the other depending on the product). The reset is complete when the LEDs stop blinking, and the light comes on if one is fitted. Written for current-firmware fans; not established for legacy firmware or for the infrared remote.
procedures.indicator: Fan LEDs blink rapidly, then stop. A fitted light comes on.
procedures.name: Remote: hold Fan Power, then tap a speed key

steps.action: Press and hold Fan Power on the remote for about 5 seconds, until the fan's LEDs start blinking and it beeps.
Tap Speed Minus (or Speed Plus, depending on the product).
Wait for the LEDs to stop blinking.
steps.expect: The reset is complete. A fitted light comes on.

methods.description: Join the device's own setup Wi-Fi, find it with the normal UDP probe, and send it NW;JOIN with the home SSID and passphrase. The passphrase travels in plain text. No account and no cloud are involved. The type is softap_udp because the same request is accepted as a UDP datagram or on the TCP connection. The vendor app uses TCP, and the schema has no softap type for a raw TCP text protocol.
methods.name: Setup access point, then a join request on port 31415

steps.action: Power a device that has no Wi-Fi network stored: new, factory reset, or downgraded from 3.x. Wait for it to start its setup access point.
steps.expect: A new Wi-Fi network appears. Its name and security are not established.

steps.action: Join the client to the device's setup access point.
Broadcast <ALL;DEVICE;ID;GET> to UDP 31415 on that network and read the device's MAC and model from the reply.
Optionally ask the device to scan for networks.
steps.notes: The current vendor app sends this. The reply format is not established. Skip it and ask the user for the SSID instead.

steps.action: Send the home SSID and passphrase with NW;JOIN, escaping both.
steps.expect: The device leaves its setup network and joins the home network. No reply format is established.
steps.notes: The vendor app sends this on its TCP connection to port 31415. The body is the same either way.

steps.action: Return the client to the home network and repeat discovery there.
Broadcast the probe on the home network and confirm the device answers with the same MAC.
steps.expect: The device answers from its new home-network address.

causes: A wrong passphrase. No join result is established on the wire, so the only sign of failure is the device returning to its setup network, if it does at all.
The home network is 5 GHz-only or uses client isolation. The Wi-Fi band the module supports is not established.
The client is still on the setup network, or the phone OS is keeping it there because that network has no internet.
troubleshooting.symptom: The device never answers on the home network.

methods.description: The vendor's older app, which the current Big Ass Fans app names as the one legacy products are designed for. It performs the same setup-access-point exchange. Whether it can still be installed is not established. Do not use the current Big Ass Fans app for this if the goal is to stay on this protocol: it offers a firmware update that moves the device to 3.x.
methods.name: Vendor app: Haiku by BAF

steps.action: Install Haiku by BAF (or the older Haiku Home) and add the product. The app walks through joining the device's setup network.
steps.expect: The device appears on the home network and answers the UDP probe.

steps.action: Decline any firmware update offered by the current Big Ass Fans app if the device must stay on SenseME.

setup.notes: A legacy device joins Wi-Fi from its own setup access point. Evidence: GETALL reports NW;AP;STATUS (OFF on every provisioned device in the published dumps) and NW;DHCP. The current vendor app's legacy-device handler can send a Wi-Fi scan request and a join request carrying SSID and passphrase, then tells the user the device "was instructed to join" the new network. Not established: the setup AP's SSID, its security, the device's address on it, and how a factory-fresh device signals that it is in setup mode. Nothing here has been replayed. The exchange is the same protocol and port as normal control, so any client that can send one command can provision.

rejoin.notes: While the device is still reachable, send wifi_join with the new SSID and passphrase. It leaves the current network and joins the new one. The current vendor app's legacy handler does exactly this and then tells the user to move the phone to the new network. The old network must still be up when the join is sent. After a router has already been replaced, the only route is a factory reset and the setup-access-point method. Reported from the vendor app; not replayed.

steps.action: Send wifi_join with the new SSID and passphrase to the device on the current network.
Move the client to the new network and rediscover the device by MAC.

testing.notes: Not driven against hardware by this project, and no capture of real traffic is held in the research store. The wire grammar, reply shapes and ranges come from open-source clients that were written against real fans (aiosenseme, the Indigo plugin, TomFaulkner/SenseMe, openHAB). The vendor-app facts come from a static reading of Big Ass Fans 3.3.4 and 3.4.0. Both kinds of source are `reported`, not `confirmed`.

entities.name: Fan
entities.notes: State paths in this file are SenseME reply keys: the tokens between the device name and the value, joined with ';' (see payload_formats.SenseMEReply). Speed is a step 0-7, not a percentage. A consumer mapping a percentage slider should use FAN;SPD;MAX (7) and round. Direction is its own select entity below.

entities.name: Light
entities.notes: The fan's light kit. Draw it only when DEVICE;LIGHT reports PRESENT. Brightness is a step 0-16 (LIGHT;LEVEL;MAX).

entities.name: Haiku Light
entities.notes: Standalone Haiku Light. Colour temperature is in kelvin, 2200-5000.

entities.name: Direction
entities.notes: REV is the vendor's winter / Heat Assist direction.

entities.name: Smart Mode
entities.notes: The configured mode. SMARTMODE;ACTUAL (read-only) is the one currently in effect.

entities.name: Smart Cooling Target
entities.notes: Hundredths of a degree Celsius on the wire. Apps that show Fahrenheit write values like 2388 (75 F), which is why the step is 0.01.

entities.name: Occupancy
entities.notes: Not in GETALL: read with get_occupancy on connect, then follow pushes. On the Haiku L, and apparently the Haiku Light, check DEVICE;OPTION;SENSORS first. The Haiku Light dump reports NOT PRESENT and still reports a status, so treat its reading with suspicion. The wall control reports occupancy too.

entities.name: Occupancy Timeout
entities.notes: Milliseconds on the wire. How long after the last motion the motion-triggered fan and light switch off.

entities.name: Identify
entities.notes: Vendor-app message only; the signal it produces on legacy firmware is not established.

entities.name: Room
entities.notes: Room name, or EMPTY when the device is not in a room. Devices sharing a name here are one vendor-app room.

evidence.app_static_analysis: Big Ass Fans for Android 3.3.4 and 3.4.0 (listing updated 2025-12-01), read statically. The app still has a handler for legacy SenseME devices. It builds requests as <target;category;attribute;args...> (GETALL as <target;GETALL>), broadcasts <ALL;DEVICE;ID;GET> on UDP 31415 to the subnet-directed address every 5 s from a socket bound to local port 31415, and talks to a found device over a TCP connection to port 31415 with a 10 s connect timeout. It knows the model strings FAN,HAIKU,SENSEME, FAN,HAIKU,HSERIES, FAN,LSERIES, LIGHT,HAIKU, SWITCH,SENSEME and "Speakeasy". Beyond the community vocabulary, it sends NW;SCAN, NW;JOIN;ssid;passphrase, NAME;VALUE;SET;name, DEVICE;SIGNAL;SET;10000, FW;NAME;GET, FW;<family>;GET and a bare GROUP;LIST. It escapes < > ; ( ) + , and backslash in free text. Its firmware path for legacy devices requests "-GEN3" (3.x) images and uploads over plain HTTP to port 31416. Its strings include a support-only downgrade to the Haiku app, which factory-resets the device. NEGATIVE FINDING: the *CLUSTERMESSAGE, *COMMAND, FANMAXSPEED and SLEEPFANSPEED names listed in the research notes are protobuf field and payload-case names of the 3.x protocol. They are not SenseME tokens.

artifacts.artifact: Big Ass Fans for Android (com.baf.i6) 3.3.4 and 3.4.0 (3.4.0 SHA-256 2d5985ef7cb9b29b2e0543fba0312766343c70e7be1293001c54e02a768a382b)
artifacts.description: Established that the current app still speaks SenseME to legacy devices, and supplied the join, scan, rename and identify messages, the escaping rule and the firmware path. Protocol facts only; no vendor code, symbols or strings beyond short paraphrase.
Discovery, framing, reply parsing, set vocabulary, GETALL dumps from five models.
Original traffic-derived client; UDP set datagrams; validation ranges.

artifacts.artifact: TomFaulkner/SenseMe, sean9keenan/BigAssFansAPI, forty2/haiku-senseme, openHAB bigassfan binding
artifacts.description: Cross-checks: GET-with-qualifier spelling, units for occupancy timeout and height, TIME;VALUE format, OUI.

evidence.open_questions: Setup access point SSID, security and address. The reply to NW;JOIN and NW;SCAN. A factory reset that is known to work on legacy firmware. Whether the device checks the request's target token on a unicast connection. Whether discovery replies are unicast to the probe's source port. The unit of FAN;TIMER and of the identify duration. The schedule event format. The WINTERMODE;STATE write spelling. Whether a legacy room-temperature or humidity GET exists. What the "Speakeasy" model is. Whether a 3.x device also answers the ASCII UDP probe.
evidence.public_implementations: aiosenseme (archived 2023-06-09 at commit a48d4db) is the most complete client. Its discovery.py and device.py give the probe, the reply filter, the TCP lifecycle, the reply splitter with its per-key value counts and the set vocabulary with client-side clamps. Its data/ directory holds GETALL dumps from a Haiku fan, a Haiku L fan with and without the wireless wall switch, a Haiku Light and a wall control, all on 2.5.x firmware. The Indigo plugin (commit 038b581) is the original traffic-derived client: TCP for state, a UDP datagram per set command, and explicit validation ranges (speed 0-7, light 0-16, Smart cooling minimum 0-6 and maximum 1-7, sleep temperature 10-32 C). TomFaulkner/ SenseMe adds the GET-with-qualifier spelling, the occupancy-timeout unit (ms) and the fan-height write. BigAssFansAPI documents the height unit and the older LEARN;STATE key. haiku-senseme's commands.json is an independent key catalogue. The openHAB binding documents the TIME;VALUE format and three device MACs sharing the 20:F8:5E OUI. All of these were written against real fans. None of their captures is held here.

enter.notes: The app uploads to the running device. No separate bootloader entry command is known.

image.notes: The vendor app fetches images from the vendor cloud with a token-gated download tied to an account and a claimed device, then relays them to the device over the LAN. No image is held. For the legacy firmware families (FW000004 to FW000007) the current app asks the cloud for a "-GEN3" image, i.e. firmware 3.x. It has no mapping for FW000003, the family on the Haiku fan in aiosenseme's dump, and what it does for that family is not established.

dfu.notes: ONE-WAY FOR THIS PROTOCOL. Accepting an update from the current Big Ass Fans app moves a legacy device to firmware 3.x, which no longer speaks SenseME (openHAB, aiosenseme and owners' reviews all record integrations breaking this way). The app also carries a support-directed "Downgrade to Haiku App" path. Per the app's own text, it reinstalls legacy firmware and factory-resets the device, which then has to be set up again with the Haiku app. The upload itself is plain HTTP to TCP port 31416 on the device (reported, from the app). Its paths, bodies and framing are deliberately not recorded here. A client that wants to keep a device on this protocol should never trigger an update.

http_endpoints.description: Placeholder only. Nothing here is an HTTP control endpoint. Control is the ASCII SenseME protocol on TCP and UDP port 31415 (see protocol_details.senseme and the commands below).
http_endpoints.name: Local API Placeholder

initialization.description: Learn the MAC and model string. aiosenseme sends this first on every connection.
GETALL does not report the occupancy sensor, so ask for it explicitly (aiosenseme, Indigo).
Read every setting. The burst ends with no terminator. aiosenseme treats a fan's WINTERMODE;STATE reply, or a light's SNSROCC;TIMEOUT;MIN, as the end of the first full update.

Bookends.description: FAN;BOOKENDS and LIGHT;BOOKENDS: a room-level min;max pair.

fields.description: Lowest step the room allows (speed step for the fan, brightness step for the light).
fields.name: min

parse_rules: Two values. min must be below max; aiosenseme refuses to send min >= max.

CentiCelsius.description: LEARN;ZEROTEMP and SMARTSLEEP;IDEALTEMP: a temperature target as an integer in hundredths of a degree Celsius.

fields.description: value = raw x 0.01. Always Celsius on the wire; clients convert for display.
fields.name: temperature

parse_rules: Parse as a decimal integer and multiply by 0.01. Round writes to the nearest integer after dividing by 0.01. The app's Fahrenheit targets produce values such as 2388 (75 F).

DiscoveryReply.description: The single UDP datagram a device sends in answer to the discovery probe, and the reply to get_device_id on a TCP connection. Strip the outer parentheses first.

fields.description: User-assigned device name, escaped as in protocol_details.senseme.escaping.
fields.name: name

fields.description: Wi-Fi MAC, upper-case hex, colon-separated. The stable identity and the target for every later request.
fields.name: mac

fields.description: Comma-separated model family, e.g. FAN,HAIKU,SENSEME. Matched against device.variants[].identification.model_prefix.
fields.name: model

parse_rules: Drop the datagram unless it starts with '(' and ends with ')'.
Strip both, split on ';' and expect exactly five fields. aiosenseme discards anything else, and anything shorter than 31 or longer than 200 characters overall.
A name containing an escaped ';' breaks naive splitting. Split on ';' not preceded by a backslash, then unescape.
The model field is itself comma-separated. Keep it whole for matching.

NetworkParams.description: The value of NW;PARAMS;ACTUAL: the device's own view of its IPv4 configuration.
parse_rules: Three values. This order is what every published dump shows. aiosenseme's accessors swap fields 1 and 2; trust the dumps.

SenseMEReply.description: Every reply and every pushed state change on the control connection: a device name, a key of one or more tokens, and one or more values.
SenseMEReply.example: (Living Room Fan;FAN;SPD;ACTUAL;3)(Living Room Fan;FAN;BOOKENDS;1;7)(Living Room Fan;LEARN;ZEROTEMP;2388)
parse_rules: Accumulate bytes. Cut a message at each ')' that is not preceded by a backslash. Keep any tail after the last cut for the next read.
Each message must start with '('. Strip the outer parentheses.
Split on unescaped ';'. Token 0 is the device name.
Look the remaining tokens up in protocol_details.senseme.value_counts: that many trailing tokens are values and the rest is the key. Default one value.
A key of ERROR is a rejected request. Log it; its value is not documented.
A key of TIME;VALUE is the device clock (ISO-8601 UTC); aiosenseme ignores it for change detection because it moves every read.

connection_lifecycle: Open TCP 31415. Send get_device_id, get_occupancy and get_all (see initialization).
Keep the connection open. Every change arrives as a reply-shaped push, whatever made it.

aiosenseme re-sends DEVICE;ID;GET, SNSROCC;STATUS;GET and GETALL about once a minute, with jitter, and aborts the connection after about 90 s of silence (refresh interval + 30 s). The Indigo plugin re-initialises after a configurable number of silent minutes.
On a lost connection, reconnect after a short delay. aiosenseme waits 1 s after a drop and 60 s after a refused connect.
Several clients may be connected at once. Do not assume a write came from this client; read the push.

escaping.rule: Free-text values (the device name, an SSID, a passphrase) put a backslash before each of these eight characters. This is the vendor app's rule. aiosenseme's reply splitter honours backslash escapes on the way back. Keys and enumerated values never need escaping.

models.FAN,HAIKU,HSERIES: Haiku H series. aiosenseme treats it as the same Haiku fan.
models.FAN,HAIKU,SENSEME: Haiku fan with SenseME. Occupancy sensor fitted; light kit optional (DEVICE;LIGHT).
models.FAN,LSERIES: Haiku L with the Wi-Fi module. Sensor presence reported by DEVICE;OPTION;SENSORS.
models.SWITCH,SENSEME: Haiku Wall Control. Has an occupancy sensor. aiosenseme ignores it in discovery; its state is reflected through the fans it controls.
models.notes: The model field is a comma-separated list. aiosenseme treats an unknown model as a fan. The current vendor app's legacy handler also accepts the string "Speakeasy", which it draws with Haiku Luxe line art. No open-source client has seen it; its wire behaviour is a hypothesis. "FAN,HAIKU,CBE" appears only in the app's 3.x handler and is not a legacy discovery reply.

ports.notes: Discovery is UDP. Control is normally one long-lived TCP connection, which is the only way to receive pushed changes. The Indigo plugin shows a set command also works as one UDP datagram to port 31415. The vendor app connects with a 10 s connect timeout. openHAB and the Indigo plugin enable TCP keepalive (Indigo: 60 s).

rules: A reply starts with '(' and ends with the first ')' that is not preceded by a backslash. Several replies can arrive back to back with nothing between them, and a TCP read can end partway through one. Keep the tail for the next read.
Split the inside on ';'. Token 0 is the device's name. openHAB's parser also accepts the MAC there, so compare it to neither; the connection already says which device this is.

The remaining tokens are a KEY followed by one or more VALUES. How many trailing tokens are values depends on the key. Most keys have one; the exceptions are in value_counts. A parser that does not know the key cannot split it reliably.
A key of ERROR reports a rejected request. Its value is not documented; aiosenseme logs it and moves on.
Values are ASCII: ON/OFF, integers in decimal, enumerated words, or free text with the escaping below.

value_counts.DEVICE;LIGHT: variable: PRESENT, NOT PRESENT, or PRESENT;COLOR on the Haiku Light, whose reply key is DEVICE;LIGHT;PRESENT with value COLOR
value_counts.FW;<fw name>: 1, but the key itself carries the firmware family token from FW;NAME (for example FW;FW000003)
value_counts.NW;PARAMS;ACTUAL: 3 (address;netmask;gateway in the published dumps; aiosenseme labels fields 1 and 2 the other way round, which the dumps contradict)

request_grammar.encoding: ASCII (clients encode UTF-8). Every other byte is literal, with no length prefix, checksum or line terminator.
request_grammar.spelling_variants: Clients disagree on a few boolean writes. The Indigo plugin and aiosenseme send FAN;AUTO;ON while TomFaulkner sends FAN;AUTO;SET;ON. For Smart Mode, aiosenseme and Indigo write SMARTMODE;STATE;SET;<mode> while BigAssFansAPI and TomFaulkner drive an older LEARN;STATE key whose "on" value is the word LEARN. openHAB sends FAN;WINTERMODE;ON but reads WINTERMODE;STATE. This file declares the spelling that at least two independent clients share and leaves the rest here.
request_grammar.target: The first token picks the device. Clients use the MAC as the device reports it (upper-case, colon-separated), the device name, or ALL (the discovery probe and BigAssFansAPI's broadcast). aiosenseme's first unicast request uses the IP address. On a unicast connection the device therefore accepts more than its own MAC here, and whether it checks the token at all is not established. Use the MAC.

verbs.meaning: Switch a boolean. Examples: FAN;PWR;ON, LIGHT;AUTO;OFF, FAN;WHOOSH;ON.
Write a value. Examples: FAN;SPD;SET;3, FAN;BOOKENDS;SET;2;6.

Read one value. The qualifier (ACTUAL, MIN, MAX, CURR, STATUS) comes AFTER GET on the request, though the reply puts it before the value: <T;FAN;SPD;GET;ACTUAL> is answered with (name;FAN;SPD;ACTUAL;3). Keys without a qualifier take a bare GET (FAN;PWR;GET). Spelling from TomFaulkner/SenseMe.
Dump every setting as a burst of replies. The occupancy status is not included.

senseme.rooms: Legacy "rooms" (the vendor app's fan and light groups) are stored on each device as GROUP;LIST (room name) and GROUP;ROOM;TYPE, together with the FAN;BOOKENDS and LIGHT;BOOKENDS room limits. No room-wide command is established. The published clients address one device at a time, and aiosenseme finds a room's members by matching GROUP;LIST across discovered devices. NEGATIVE FINDING: RESEARCH.md listed FANCLUSTERMESSAGE, LIGHTCLUSTERMESSAGE, FANSTEPCOMMAND, LIGHTLEVELCONTROLCOMMAND, FANMAXSPEED and SLEEPFANSPEED as SenseME vocabulary. In the vendor app they are field and payload-case names of the 3.x protobuf messages, not ASCII tokens. None of them appears on the legacy wire.

DEVICE;LIGHT.notes: Whether a light kit is fitted. Draw light controls only when PRESENT.

DEVICE;OPTION;SENSORS.notes: Haiku L and Haiku Light: whether the sensor board is fitted. The Haiku Light dump reports NOT PRESENT and still reports SNSROCC;STATUS.

DEVICE;SERVER.notes: Which vendor cloud environment the device uses.

ERRORLOG;ENTRIES;NUM.notes: Error-log entry count (MAX 10). How to read entries is not established.

FAN;AUTO.notes: The fan switches on with motion.

FAN;BOOKENDS.notes: Room-level speed limits min;max (1;7 by default). The number of steps stays the same inside the limits.

FAN;DIR.notes: REV is the vendor's winter or Heat Assist direction.

FAN;SPD;ACTUAL.notes: Speed step. 0 = stopped. Bounded by FAN;SPD;MIN/MAX (1 and 7 in every dump).

FAN;SPD;MAX.notes: Highest speed step, read-only. 7 in every dump. Clamp writes to this, never to a constant.

FAN;SPD;MIN.notes: Lowest running speed step, read-only. 1 in every dump.

FAN;TIMER;CURR.notes: Fan timer. MIN 1 and MAX 7 in the dumps. The unit is not established.

FAN;WHOOSH;STATUS.notes: Whoosh varies speed around the current setting. aiosenseme observed that setting a speed turns it off.

FW;NAME.notes: Firmware family token: FW000003 (Haiku fan), FW000004 (wall control), FW000005 (Haiku L), FW000006 (Haiku Light) in the dumps. The vendor app also knows FW000007.

GROUP;LIST.notes: Room name, or EMPTY when the device is in no room.

GROUP;ROOM;TYPE.notes: Room category code. 0 = not in a room; 1-28 are vendor room categories (bedroom, kitchen, patio and so on). aiosenseme's device.py lists the labels. Cosmetic.

LEARN;MAXSPEED.notes: Smart cooling highest speed. 7 = no maximum. Indigo validates 1-7.

LEARN;MINSPEED.notes: Smart cooling lowest speed. 0 = no minimum. Indigo validates 0-6.

LEARN;ZEROTEMP.notes: Cooling target in hundredths of a degree Celsius, always Celsius on the wire. 2111 = 21.11 C = 70 F.

LIGHT;AUTO.notes: The light switches on with motion.

LIGHT;BOOKENDS.notes: Room-level brightness limits min;max (1;16). No published client writes it.

LIGHT;COLOR;LEVEL;VALUE.notes: Haiku Light only, 1-10 with 5 observed. Meaning not established.

LIGHT;COLOR;TEMP;VALUE.notes: Haiku Light only. Bounded by LIGHT;COLOR;TEMP;MIN/MAX (2200 and 5000 K). aiosenseme rounds writes to 100 K.

LIGHT;LEVEL;ACTUAL.notes: Brightness step, bounded by LIGHT;LEVEL;MIN/MAX (1 and 16).

LIGHT;MODE.notes: Haiku Light only. Other values not established.

NW;AP;STATUS.notes: Whether the device's own access point is up. OFF once provisioned. TomFaulkner reads it as NW;AP;GET;STATUS.

NW;DHCP.notes: Whether the device runs a DHCP server, presumably on its setup access point. OFF once provisioned.

NW;RSSI.notes: Seen in the Haiku Light dump only.

NW;SSID.notes: The Wi-Fi network the device is on.

NW;TOKEN.notes: Per-device UUID, 8-4-4-4-12 hex. aiosenseme uses it as the device's uuid.

SCHEDULE;CAP.notes: 'MAX EVENTS,29' in every dump: up to 29 schedule events.

SCHEDULE;EVENT;LIST.notes: NONE when empty. The schedule event format is not established.

SLEEP;EVENT.notes: Meaning not established. aiosenseme suppresses callbacks for it.

SLEEP;EVENT;OFF.notes: What the light does when sleep mode ends (TomFaulkner: wake-up brightness). Comma-separated inside one value.

SMARTMODE;ACTUAL.notes: The mode currently in effect. Read-only.

SMARTMODE;STATE.notes: The configured Smart Mode (the vendor's Auto Comfort). FOLLOWTSTAT follows a linked thermostat's mode.

SMARTSLEEP;IDEALTEMP.notes: Sleep-mode target, hundredths of a degree Celsius.

SNSROCC;STATUS.notes: Motion sensor. Not in GETALL; ask with get_occupancy. Pushed on change on an open connection (Indigo triggers on it).

SNSROCC;TIMEOUT;CURR.notes: No-motion auto-off delay. MIN 60000 (1 min), MAX 86400000 (24 h).

TIME;VALUE.notes: Device clock as ISO-8601 UTC, e.g. 2017-03-26T14:06:27Z (openHAB).

WALLCONTROL;CONFIGURE;FANSPEED.notes: Wall control only. LIGHTLEVEL observed. Meaning not established.

WINTERMODE;HEIGHT.notes: Fan mounting height used by winter mode. 213 = 7 ft, 274 = 9 ft. TomFaulkner writes WINTERMODE;HEIGHT;SET;<cm>.

WINTERMODE;STATE.notes: Winter (heating) mode. The write spelling is disputed between clients; not declared.

vendor_app_only.DEVICE;SIGNAL;SET;10000: Identify. The app's locate action sends 10000; the unit is not established (plausibly milliseconds). Declared as `identify`.
vendor_app_only.FW;NAME;GET then FW;<family>;GET: Firmware family and version. Both keys are also in GETALL.
vendor_app_only.GROUP;LIST: Sent bare, with no GET, to learn the room when firmware info is missing.
vendor_app_only.NW;JOIN;<ssid>;<passphrase>: Join a network. Both fields escaped. Declared as `wifi_join`.
vendor_app_only.NW;SCAN: Ask the device to scan for Wi-Fi networks. Reply format not established. Declared as `wifi_scan`.

remaining_unknowns: The setup access point: SSID pattern, open or secured, the device's address on it, and how a factory-fresh or reset device indicates it is in setup mode.
Replies to NW;JOIN and NW;SCAN, and how a failed join shows itself.
A factory reset procedure verified on legacy firmware (the candidate here is the current app's remote sequence).
Whether the target token is checked on a unicast connection (aiosenseme sends the IP address there once and gets an answer).
Whether discovery replies go to the probe's source port, to 31415, or to broadcast.
The unit of FAN;TIMER (MIN 1, MAX 7) and of DEVICE;SIGNAL's 10000.
The schedule event format behind SCHEDULE;EVENT;LIST (up to 29 events).
The WINTERMODE;STATE write spelling (openHAB and BigAssFansAPI disagree).
Whether any legacy key reports room temperature or humidity. No published client reads one.
What LIGHT;COLOR;LEVEL, LIGHT;MODE, SLEEP;EVENT and WALLCONTROL;CONFIGURE;FANSPEED control.
Which hardware reports the 'Speakeasy' model string, and whether 3.x devices answer the ASCII UDP probe at all.
Whether the current app's missing firmware mapping for FW000003 (Haiku fan) means those fans are updated some other way or not at all.
